name: Mountain Pose
benefits: Builds awareness of standing posture and alignment
Gently engages the legs and core
A calm starting point for every standing sequence
instructions: Stand with your feet hip width apart or big toes touching, weight spread evenly over both feet.
Lift and spread your toes, then place them down and press through the whole foot.
Gently firm your thighs and lengthen your tailbone toward the floor.
Lift your chest, relax your shoulders down and back, and let your arms hang with palms facing forward.
Keep your chin level and the crown of your head reaching up. Breathe slowly.
breathing: Breathe in and out through the nose, letting each inhale lengthen the spine.
beginner_modification: Stand with your back against a wall to feel your alignment, feet a little wider apart.
advanced_variation: Close your eyes to challenge balance, or raise your arms overhead into Upward Salute.
common_mistakes: Leaning back with the ribs flaring forward
Lifting the shoulders toward the ears
safety_tips: Keep a soft bend in the knees if they tend to hyperextend.
Hold onto a wall or chair if you feel unsteady.
contraindications: Recent dizziness or low blood pressure when standing still for long periods

name: Upward Salute
benefits: Stretches the sides of the body and the shoulders
Encourages an upright, open posture
A gentle energizing movement for the start of the day
instructions: Start in Mountain Pose with your arms by your sides.
As you breathe in, sweep your arms out to the sides and up overhead.
Keep your arms shoulder width apart or bring the palms together.
Lengthen up through the fingertips while keeping your shoulders away from your ears.
As you breathe out, lower your arms back down. Repeat with the breath.
breathing: Inhale as the arms rise, exhale as they lower.
duration: 3 to 5 breaths at the top, or 6 to 10 slow repetitions
beginner_modification: Raise the arms only as high as your shoulders allow, or keep the palms apart.
advanced_variation: Add a gentle side bend to each side at the top.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to get the arms higher
safety_tips: Keep the movement within a pain free range for the shoulders.
contraindications: Recent shoulder injury or surgery (check with your physiotherapist)

name: Standing Forward Fold
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves
Lets the spine and neck release downward
Often feels calming at the end of a standing sequence
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose with your feet hip width apart.
Breathe in and lengthen your spine; breathe out and hinge forward from the hips.
Bend your knees as much as you need so your belly can rest toward your thighs.
Let your head and arms hang, or hold opposite elbows.
To come up, bend the knees, place the hands on the hips and rise slowly with a long back.
breathing: Breathe out as you fold; let each exhale soften you a little deeper.
beginner_modification: Keep the knees generously bent and rest the hands on blocks or your shins.
advanced_variation: Straighten the legs gradually and bring the palms flat beside the feet.
common_mistakes: Rounding from the upper back instead of hinging at the hips
safety_tips: Rise slowly to avoid dizziness.
Bend the knees if you feel strain in the lower back.
contraindications: Glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure (head below heart)

name: Half Forward Fold
benefits: Teaches a long, neutral spine while hinging
Stretches the backs of the legs
Links forward folds smoothly in a flow
instructions: From Standing Forward Fold, place your hands on your shins or on blocks.
Breathe in and lift your chest forward until your back is long and flat.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears and look slightly ahead of your feet.
Breathe out and fold back down, or hold for a few breaths.
breathing: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to fold.
beginner_modification: Bend the knees and place the hands higher on the thighs.
advanced_variation: Keep the legs straight with the fingertips on the floor.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head too high and pinching the neck
safety_tips: Keep a micro bend in the knees.

name: Tree Pose
benefits: Improves balance and focus
Strengthens the standing leg and ankle
Opens the hip of the lifted leg
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto your left foot.
Place the sole of your right foot on your left ankle, calf or inner thigh, not on the knee.
Press the foot and leg into each other and point the right knee out to the side.
Bring your palms together at your chest, or raise your arms overhead.
Fix your gaze on a still point and breathe. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Slow, even breaths; if you wobble, keep breathing rather than holding the breath.
beginner_modification: Keep the toes of the lifted foot on the floor with the heel against the ankle, or hold a wall.
advanced_variation: Raise the arms overhead and slowly close your eyes.
common_mistakes: Pressing the foot into the side of the knee
Hip of the standing leg jutting out to the side
safety_tips: Practise near a wall or chair.
Never place the foot directly on the knee joint.
contraindications: Recent ankle or knee injury on the standing leg
Vertigo or balance disorders without support

name: Warrior I
target_areas: Hip flexors of the back leg
benefits: Strengthens the legs and glutes
Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg
Builds stamina and an open chest
instructions: From Mountain Pose, step your left foot back about one leg length.
Turn the back foot out about 45 degrees and press the outer edge down.
Bend the front knee until it is over the ankle; keep the back leg straight.
Square your hips toward the front as much as is comfortable.
Raise your arms overhead and lengthen up through the spine. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Inhale as the arms rise, then breathe steadily while holding.
beginner_modification: Shorten the stance and keep the hands on the hips.
advanced_variation: Bend the front knee to 90 degrees and bring the palms together overhead.
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting past the toes or inward
Feet on one line (a tightrope stance)
safety_tips: Keep the front knee tracking over the second toe.
Widen the stance side to side for balance.
contraindications: Shoulder injury (keep the hands on the hips)

name: Warrior II
benefits: Strengthens the legs and builds stamina
Opens the hips and inner thighs
Strengthens the shoulders and improves focus
instructions: Stand with your feet wide apart, about the length of one leg.
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in slightly.
Raise your arms to shoulder height, palms down.
Bend the right knee over the right ankle while the left leg stays straight.
Keep the torso upright, look over the right hand and breathe. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Steady, even breathing; lengthen the arms on each inhale.
beginner_modification: Bend the front knee less and rest the hands on the hips.
advanced_variation: Lower the front thigh until it is parallel to the floor.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso over the front leg
safety_tips: Keep the front knee over the ankle, not past the toes.
contraindications: Recent knee, hip or groin injury

name: Low Lunge
benefits: Stretches tight hip flexors from long sitting
Opens the front of the hips and thighs
Builds balance and steadiness close to the floor
instructions: From Downward Facing Dog or tabletop, step your right foot forward between your hands.
Lower your left knee to the mat and slide it back a little.
Stack the right knee over the right ankle.
Lift your chest and raise your arms, or rest your hands on your front thigh.
Gently move the hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the left hip. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Inhale to lift the chest, exhale to soften the hips forward.
beginner_modification: Place a folded blanket under the back knee and keep the hands on blocks.
advanced_variation: Reach the arms overhead and hold the back foot for a quad stretch.
common_mistakes: Front knee travelling past the toes
safety_tips: Pad the back knee.
Keep the stretch moderate; it should not pinch the front of the hip.

name: Chair Pose
benefits: Builds strength in the thighs and glutes
Raises the heart rate in a short hold
Trains core control and posture
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose with your feet together or hip width apart.
Breathe in and raise your arms overhead.
Breathe out and bend your knees as if sitting back into a chair.
Keep your weight in your heels and your knees behind your toes.
Lengthen the spine with the chest lifted; hold, then straighten the legs to come up.
breathing: Keep breathing steadily; the hold should feel strong but not breathless.
beginner_modification: Bend the knees less and keep the hands on the hips or in front of the chest.
advanced_variation: Sit lower until the thighs approach parallel and add a twist.
safety_tips: Keep the knees in line with the toes.

name: Child's Pose
benefits: Gently stretches the lower back, hips and thighs
A natural resting pose between harder poses
Slow breathing here often feels calming
instructions: Kneel on the mat with your big toes touching and your knees together or apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead on the mat or on a block.
Keep the arms long in front of you or rest them alongside your body. Breathe into your back.
breathing: Feel the back of the ribs expand on each inhale; relax a little more on each exhale.
recommended_repetitions: As often as needed for rest
beginner_modification: Place a cushion between your hips and heels, or under your chest.
advanced_variation: Walk the hands to one side for a side body stretch.
safety_tips: Widen the knees if the belly feels compressed.
Use padding under the knees if needed.
contraindications: Knee injury or pain when kneeling
Late pregnancy (use wide knees and support, or skip)

name: Cat-Cow
benefits: Moves the spine through flexion and extension
A gentle warm up for the back and neck
Links movement with the breath
instructions: Start on hands and knees: wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe in for Cow: let the belly drop, lift the chest and tailbone, look slightly forward.
Breathe out for Cat: press the floor away, round the spine up and tuck the chin.
Move slowly between the two, one breath per movement.
breathing: Inhale into Cow, exhale into Cat.
beginner_modification: Do it seated in a chair with the hands on the knees.
advanced_variation: Add hip circles or move each vertebra in sequence.
safety_tips: Keep the range small if the back is stiff.
Make fists or use a wedge if the wrists hurt.
contraindications: Recent neck or back injury (keep the range very small or skip)

name: Downward-Facing Dog
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, calves and spine
Builds strength in the arms and shoulders
A key transition pose that links many sequences
instructions: Start on hands and knees with your hands slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes, breathe out and lift your knees off the floor.
Send your hips up and back so your body makes an upside down V.
Spread your fingers, press the floor away and let your head hang between your arms.
Keep the knees bent at first; straighten them gradually as the hamstrings allow.
breathing: Long, slow breaths; press the floor away on each exhale.
beginner_modification: Keep the knees bent and the heels lifted, or place the hands on a chair seat.
advanced_variation: Lift one leg toward the ceiling (three legged dog).
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to straighten the legs
safety_tips: Bend the knees freely.
Spread pressure through the whole hand to protect the wrists.
contraindications: Uncontrolled high blood pressure or glaucoma (head below heart)

name: Puppy Pose
benefits: Opens the shoulders and upper back
A gentle alternative to Downward Dog
Releases tension from hunching over screens
instructions: Start on hands and knees with your hips over your knees.
Walk your hands forward, keeping the hips stacked over the knees.
Lower your chest and forehead toward the mat.
Keep the arms active and let the chest melt down. Breathe slowly.
breathing: Breathe into the upper back and let the chest soften on the exhale.
beginner_modification: Rest the forehead on a block and keep the arms wider.
advanced_variation: Bring the palms together and bend the elbows behind the head.
common_mistakes: Hips sinking back toward the heels
safety_tips: Pad the knees.
Keep the stretch gentle in the shoulders.

name: Cobra Pose
benefits: Strengthens the muscles along the spine
Opens the chest and front of the body
Counters long periods of sitting and slouching
instructions: Lie on your front with your legs together and the tops of your feet on the mat.
Place your hands under your shoulders and hug the elbows in close to your body.
Press the tops of the feet and the pubic bone down.
Breathe in and lift your chest, using your back muscles more than your arms.
Keep the elbows bent and the neck long, then lower down as you breathe out.
breathing: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower.
beginner_modification: Stay low in Baby Cobra with the hands barely pressing, or try Sphinx Pose.
advanced_variation: Lift the hands off the floor for a few breaths to build back strength.
common_mistakes: Pushing up with straight arms and crunching the lower back
safety_tips: Only lift as high as feels comfortable in the lower back.

name: Sphinx Pose
benefits: A gentle, supported backbend
Encourages extension after long sitting
Easier to hold than Cobra
instructions: Lie on your front with your legs hip width apart.
Place your elbows under your shoulders with the forearms parallel.
Press the forearms down and lift the chest forward and up.
Relax the glutes and lengthen the tailbone toward the heels. Breathe.
breathing: Calm breaths, feeling the belly press into the mat.
beginner_modification: Slide the elbows further forward to reduce the backbend.
advanced_variation: Move into Cobra Pose.
safety_tips: Back off if you feel pinching in the lower back.

name: Bridge Pose
benefits: Strengthens the glutes, hamstrings and back
Stretches the front of the hips and chest
A beginner friendly backbend
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat, hip width apart, close to your hips.
Place your arms alongside your body, palms down.
Press into your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Keep the knees pointing forward and the weight on your shoulders, not your neck.
Hold, then roll down slowly one vertebra at a time.
breathing: Inhale to lift, breathe steadily in the hold, exhale to roll down.
beginner_modification: Place a block under the sacrum for a supported bridge.
advanced_variation: Lift one leg toward the ceiling, or move toward Wheel Pose.
common_mistakes: Pushing the hips up with the lower back
safety_tips: Keep the neck still and look straight up.

name: Easy Pose
benefits: A comfortable seat for breathing and meditation
Gently opens the hips
Encourages an upright, relaxed spine
instructions: Sit on the mat and cross your shins, with each foot under the opposite knee.
Sit on the edge of a folded blanket so your hips are higher than your knees.
Rest your hands on your knees or in your lap.
Lengthen your spine, relax your shoulders and close your eyes if you like.
Switch the cross of the legs halfway through.
breathing: Breathe naturally through the nose, then let the breath slow down.
beginner_modification: Sit on a cushion or a chair with the feet flat.
advanced_variation: Sit without props for longer meditation.
common_mistakes: Knees much higher than the hips
safety_tips: Use height under the hips if the knees or back complain.
contraindications: Knee injury that dislikes deep bending (use a chair)

name: Staff Pose
benefits: Teaches upright sitting posture
Gently activates the core and legs
The starting point for most seated poses
instructions: Sit with your legs straight out in front of you, feet together and toes pointing up.
Place your hands beside your hips and press the floor down.
Sit tall, lifting the chest and lengthening the spine.
Press the backs of the legs down and flex the feet.
breathing: Even breaths, growing taller on each inhale.
beginner_modification: Sit on a folded blanket and bend the knees slightly.
advanced_variation: Lift the hands off the floor while keeping the spine tall.
safety_tips: Sit on a blanket if your lower back rounds.

name: Seated Forward Fold
benefits: Stretches the whole back of the body
A calming pose for the end of practice
Helps maintain hamstring flexibility
instructions: Sit in Staff Pose with your legs straight in front of you.
Breathe in and raise your arms, lengthening your spine.
Breathe out and hinge forward from the hips, reaching toward your shins, ankles or feet.
Keep the spine long rather than pulling yourself down.
Relax the shoulders and breathe, folding a little more on each exhale.
breathing: Lengthen on the inhale, fold slightly deeper on the exhale.
beginner_modification: Bend the knees, sit on a blanket or loop a strap around the feet.
advanced_variation: Hold the outer edges of the feet with a long spine.
common_mistakes: Rounding the upper back to reach further
safety_tips: Never bounce or force the stretch.
contraindications: Back injury or disc problems (check with a professional)

name: Bound Angle Pose
benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs
A comfortable seated stretch
Encourages an upright spine
instructions: Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together, letting the knees fall out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles.
Draw your heels as close to your body as is comfortable.
Lengthen your spine; you may hinge forward slightly with a long back.
Let gravity, not force, lower the knees.
breathing: Relax the inner thighs on each exhale.
beginner_modification: Sit on a cushion and place blocks under the knees.
advanced_variation: Fold forward from the hips with a long spine.
common_mistakes: Pushing the knees down with the hands
safety_tips: Support the knees if there is any knee or groin discomfort.

name: Seated Side Bend
benefits: Stretches the sides of the waist and the ribs
Makes room for fuller breaths
A gentle warm up from a seated position
instructions: Sit in Easy Pose.
Place your left hand on the floor beside your left hip.
Breathe in and raise your right arm overhead.
Breathe out and lean to the left, reaching over with the right arm.
Keep both sit bones grounded. Return to centre and repeat on the other side.
breathing: Inhale to reach up, exhale to bend.
beginner_modification: Keep the raised hand on the back of the head.
advanced_variation: Hold the bend for longer and add a slight twist.
safety_tips: Move slowly and keep the neck relaxed.

name: Standing Side Bend
benefits: Stretches the sides of the body
Wakes up the spine in a new direction
Good after long sitting
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and raise both arms overhead.
Interlace the fingers or hold the left wrist with the right hand.
Breathe out and lean to the right, keeping the hips centred.
Hold for a few breaths, return through the centre and repeat on the other side.
breathing: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to bend.
beginner_modification: Keep one hand on the hip.
advanced_variation: Stand with the feet together and hold longer.
common_mistakes: Pushing the hips out too far
safety_tips: Keep the bend gentle in the lower back.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
benefits: Gently rotates and releases the spine
Stretches the outer hips and glutes
Often used to wind down before relaxation
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Stretch your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Let both knees fall slowly to the right while the shoulders stay down.
Turn your head to the left if that is comfortable.
Breathe here, then bring the knees back through centre and repeat to the left.
breathing: Long exhales help the twist soften.
beginner_modification: Place a pillow under the knees.
advanced_variation: Straighten the top leg and hold the foot.
common_mistakes: Forcing the knees to the floor
safety_tips: Keep the twist gentle and pain free.

name: Knees to Chest
benefits: Gently releases the lower back
A soothing pose after backbends
Easy to do even when tired
instructions: Lie on your back.
Draw both knees toward your chest and hold your shins or the backs of the thighs.
Let your lower back relax into the floor.
Rock gently side to side if it feels good.
breathing: Breathe into the belly against the thighs.
beginner_modification: Hug one knee at a time.
advanced_variation: Lift the head toward the knees for a core curl.
safety_tips: Hold behind the thighs if the knees are sensitive.

name: Happy Baby
benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs
Releases the lower back
A playful, relaxing pose
instructions: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your armpits.
Hold the outer edges of your feet, ankles or shins.
Stack the ankles over the knees with the soles facing the ceiling.
Gently pull the knees toward the floor and rock side to side if you like.
breathing: Slow, easy breaths.
beginner_modification: Hold the backs of the thighs or use a strap.
advanced_variation: Straighten one leg at a time.
common_mistakes: Lifting the tailbone and head off the floor
safety_tips: Keep the neck relaxed on the mat.

name: Legs Up the Wall
benefits: A restful pose that many people find soothing
Lets the legs rest after standing or running
Gentle hamstring stretch
instructions: Sit sideways with one hip touching a wall.
Swing your legs up the wall as you lie back.
Shuffle your hips as close to the wall as is comfortable.
Rest your arms by your sides and close your eyes.
breathing: Natural, slow breathing.
beginner_modification: Move the hips further from the wall and bend the knees.
advanced_variation: Place a folded blanket under the hips.
common_mistakes: Hips too close for your hamstrings
safety_tips: Come out slowly by bending the knees and rolling to the side.

name: Corpse Pose
benefits: Lets the body rest and absorb the practice
Practises full physical relaxation
A natural place for a body scan or breath awareness
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs slightly apart and the feet falling open.
Rest your arms a little away from your body with the palms facing up.
Close your eyes and let the body feel heavy.
Release control of the breath and let it be natural.
To finish, deepen the breath, roll to your right side and press up slowly.
breathing: Natural breathing, with no effort.
beginner_modification: Place a pillow under the knees and a folded blanket under the head.
advanced_variation: Add a guided body scan.
safety_tips: Lie on your side with support if lying flat is uncomfortable.
contraindications: Later pregnancy (rest on the left side instead)

name: Belly Breathing
benefits: Slows the breath, which many people find calming
Builds awareness of the diaphragm
Easy to use before sleep or after training
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit comfortably.
Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly.
Breathe in through the nose so the belly hand rises more than the chest hand.
Breathe out slowly through the nose or pursed lips and feel the belly fall.
Aim for a slightly longer exhale than inhale, for example in for 4, out for 6.
breathing: In through the nose for about 4 counts, out for about 6 counts.
beginner_modification: Breathe naturally without counting.
advanced_variation: Extend the exhale gradually.
safety_tips: Stop and breathe normally if you feel light headed.
contraindications: None for most people; return to normal breathing if dizzy

name: Alternate Nostril Breathing
benefits: A slow, structured breathing practice
Helps settle attention before meditation
Can be done anywhere while seated
instructions: Sit tall in Easy Pose or on a chair.
Rest the index and middle fingers of your right hand between the eyebrows.
Close the right nostril with the thumb and breathe in through the left.
Close the left nostril with the ring finger, release the thumb and breathe out through the right.
Breathe in through the right, switch, and breathe out through the left. That is one round.
breathing: Slow and quiet; never strain or hold the breath.
beginner_modification: Do it without the hand, just imagining the breath alternating.
advanced_variation: Lengthen each breath evenly.
safety_tips: Breathe normally if you feel light headed or congested.
contraindications: A blocked nose or cold (practise belly breathing instead)

name: Body Scan Meditation
benefits: Guides attention slowly through the body
Helps you notice and release tension
A gentle way to wind down in the evening
instructions: Lie in Corpse Pose and let the breath settle.
Bring your attention to your toes and notice any sensation without changing it.
Slowly move your attention up: feet, legs, hips, belly, chest, hands, arms, shoulders, neck, face.
When the mind wanders, gently return to the last body part you remember.
Finish with a few deeper breaths and move the fingers and toes before sitting up.
breathing: Natural breathing.
beginner_modification: Scan just the major areas in 3 minutes.
advanced_variation: Scan both sides of the body separately and slowly.
safety_tips: Sit up slowly afterwards.

name: Plank Pose
benefits: Builds core and shoulder strength
Teaches a strong, straight body line
Prepares the body for arm balances
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the hands under the shoulders.
Step the feet back one at a time until the body is in one long line.
Press the floor away, keep the shoulders over the wrists and draw the belly in.
Keep the hips level with the shoulders and look slightly ahead of the hands.
Hold, then lower the knees to rest.
breathing: Steady breathing; do not hold the breath.
beginner_modification: Lower the knees to the mat, keeping a straight line from knees to head.
advanced_variation: Lift one foot for a few breaths, or move slowly to Side Plank.
safety_tips: Lower the knees as soon as your lower back starts to sag.

name: Tabletop Balance
benefits: Trains core stability with a neutral spine
Strengthens the back and glutes
Gentle on the lower back
instructions: Start on hands and knees with a neutral spine.
Slide your right hand forward and your left leg back.
Lift them to hip and shoulder height, reaching long through the fingers and the heel.
Keep the hips level and the belly drawn in.
Hold for a few breaths, return, and switch sides.
breathing: Breathe out as you extend, keep breathing in the hold.
beginner_modification: Lift only the leg or only the arm.
advanced_variation: Draw the elbow and knee together under the body between holds.
safety_tips: Move slowly and keep the hips square.

name: Locust Pose
benefits: Strengthens the whole back of the body
Supports good posture
A safe way to build backbend strength
instructions: Lie on your front with your arms alongside your body, palms down or up.
Rest your forehead on the mat and press the tops of the feet down.
Breathe in and lift your chest, arms and legs off the floor.
Reach back through the fingertips and toes, keeping the neck long.
Hold, then lower down and rest one cheek on the mat.
breathing: Inhale to lift, steady breaths in the hold, exhale to lower.
beginner_modification: Lift only the chest, or only one leg at a time (half locust).
advanced_variation: Interlace the hands behind the back and lift them higher.
safety_tips: Keep the lift modest at first.

name: Triangle Pose
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, hips and sides of the waist
Strengthens the legs and core
Opens the chest and shoulders
instructions: Stand with the feet wide apart; turn the right foot out 90 degrees and the left foot in slightly.
Raise the arms to shoulder height.
Reach the torso out over the right leg, hinging from the hip, then tilt the right hand down.
Rest the right hand on the shin, a block or the floor; reach the left arm up.
Keep both legs straight but not locked and look up, forward or down. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Lengthen on the inhale; on the exhale, rotate the chest open a little more.
beginner_modification: Rest the lower hand high on the shin or on a block; look down to ease the neck.
advanced_variation: Bring the lower hand to the floor behind the front foot.
common_mistakes: Collapsing the side of the waist
Leaning the chest toward the floor
safety_tips: Keep a micro bend in the front knee.
Look down if the neck feels strained.

name: Extended Side Angle
benefits: Strengthens the legs and glutes
Gives a long stretch from the back heel to the fingertips
Builds stamina in standing practice
instructions: Come into Warrior II with the right knee bent.
Hinge at the right hip and bring the right forearm to the right thigh, or the hand to a block.
Reach the left arm up and then over the ear, palm facing down.
Press into the outer edge of the back foot.
Keep the chest turning up toward the ceiling. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Breathe into the long side of the body.
beginner_modification: Rest the forearm on the thigh instead of the hand on the floor.
advanced_variation: Bring the lower hand to the floor outside the front foot.
safety_tips: Keep the front knee over the ankle.

name: Reverse Warrior
benefits: Stretches the side of the body while the legs work
Adds a side bend to a standing flow
Opens the ribs for fuller breathing
instructions: From Warrior II with the right knee bent, turn the right palm up.
Breathe in and sweep the right arm up and back over your head.
Let the left hand slide lightly down the back leg.
Keep the front knee bent over the ankle.
Return to Warrior II and repeat on the other side.
breathing: Inhale to reach up and back, exhale to return.
beginner_modification: Keep the lean small.
advanced_variation: Bend the front knee deeper.
common_mistakes: Leaning the weight onto the back hand
safety_tips: Keep the neck relaxed.

name: High Lunge
benefits: Strengthens the legs and core
Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg
Builds balance in a narrow stance
instructions: From Downward Dog, step the right foot forward between the hands.
Keep the back heel lifted and the back leg straight and strong.
Bend the front knee over the ankle and rise up with the arms overhead.
Draw the belly in and lengthen the tailbone down.
Hold, then repeat on the other side.
breathing: Steady breaths; reach up on each inhale.
beginner_modification: Lower the back knee into Low Lunge.
advanced_variation: Sink the hips lower while keeping the back leg straight.
common_mistakes: Leaning back with the ribs flaring
safety_tips: Widen the stance for balance.

name: Warrior III
benefits: Builds balance and full body strength
Strengthens the standing leg and the back
Trains focus
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose with the hands on the hips.
Shift your weight onto the right foot and hinge forward from the hips.
Lift the left leg behind you as the chest lowers, until body and leg are level.
Keep the hips square to the floor and the lifted foot flexed.
Reach the arms forward or keep them on the hips. Return slowly and switch sides.
breathing: Smooth breathing; gaze at a still point on the floor.
beginner_modification: Hold the back of a chair or rest the fingertips on blocks.
advanced_variation: Reach the arms forward alongside the ears.
common_mistakes: Opening the hip of the lifted leg
Dropping the chest below the hips
safety_tips: Practise near a wall or chair.
contraindications: Ankle or knee injury on the standing leg

name: Half Moon Pose
benefits: Challenges balance and coordination
Strengthens the standing leg and hips
Opens the hips and chest
instructions: From Triangle Pose on the right side, bend the right knee and place the right hand on a block ahead of the foot.
Shift your weight into the right foot and lift the left leg until it is level with the hip.
Straighten the standing leg without locking it.
Stack the left hip over the right and reach the left arm up.
Look down or forward. Lower the leg with control and repeat on the other side.
breathing: Slow breaths keep the balance steady.
beginner_modification: Practise with your back against a wall and the hand on a tall block.
advanced_variation: Look up toward the top hand.
safety_tips: Use a block under the lower hand.
Look down to stay steady.
contraindications: Ankle or knee injury on the standing leg

name: Pyramid Pose
benefits: Deeply stretches the front leg hamstring
Builds balance in a narrow stance
Calms the mind as you fold
instructions: Stand with the right foot forward and the left foot back about one leg length, back foot angled.
Square the hips toward the front.
Place the hands on the hips and lengthen the spine.
Hinge forward over the front leg with a long back.
Bring the hands to blocks or the shin and breathe. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Lengthen on the inhale, fold on the exhale.
beginner_modification: Bend the front knee and use blocks under the hands.
advanced_variation: Bring the hands into reverse prayer behind the back.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
safety_tips: Keep a micro bend in the front knee.
contraindications: High blood pressure (keep the head higher)

name: Goddess Pose
benefits: Strengthens the legs and inner thighs
Opens the hips
Builds heat and stamina quickly
instructions: Stand with the feet wide and the toes turned out about 45 degrees.
Bend the knees, lowering the hips toward knee height.
Keep the knees pointing in the same direction as the toes.
Bend the elbows to 90 degrees with the palms forward (cactus arms).
Keep the spine upright and hold, then straighten the legs.
breathing: Steady breaths; exhale as you sink.
beginner_modification: Bend the knees less and rest the hands on the thighs.
advanced_variation: Lift the heels while holding.
safety_tips: Keep the knees over the toes.

name: Garland Pose
benefits: Opens the hips and groin
Improves ankle mobility
A comfortable resting squat once mobile
instructions: Stand with the feet a little wider than the hips, toes turned out.
Bend the knees and lower the hips toward the floor.
Bring the palms together at the chest with the elbows inside the knees.
Gently press the knees out with the elbows and lift the chest.
Hold, then press up slowly.
breathing: Breathe into the back of the body.
beginner_modification: Sit on a block or place a rolled blanket under the heels.
advanced_variation: Bring the feet closer together.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting with the back rounded
safety_tips: Use support under the hips or heels.

name: Boat Pose
benefits: Builds core strength
Strengthens the hip flexors and back
Improves balance on the sit bones
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and the feet flat; hold the backs of the thighs.
Lean back slightly with a long spine and lift the feet so the shins are level.
Reach the arms forward, palms facing each other.
If comfortable, straighten the legs to make a V shape.
Keep the chest lifted and hold, then lower the feet.
breathing: Keep breathing; holding the breath makes it harder.
beginner_modification: Keep the knees bent and hold the thighs.
advanced_variation: Lower toward the floor and lift again (boat crunches).
safety_tips: Keep the spine long; bend the knees if the back rounds.

name: Side Plank
benefits: Strengthens the sides of the waist and the shoulders
Builds balance and stability
Supports a strong, upright posture
instructions: Start in Plank Pose.
Shift onto the outer edge of the right foot and stack the left foot on top.
Roll the body open to the left with the right hand under the shoulder.
Lift the hips so the body is one straight line and reach the left arm up.
Hold, return to Plank and switch sides.
breathing: Steady breathing.
beginner_modification: Lower the bottom knee to the mat, or stagger the feet.
advanced_variation: Lift the top leg.
common_mistakes: Hand too far from the shoulder
safety_tips: Spread the fingers and press through the whole hand.

name: Dolphin Pose
benefits: Builds shoulder strength without loading the wrists
Stretches the hamstrings and calves
Prepares for forearm balances
instructions: Start on hands and knees, then lower onto the forearms with the elbows under the shoulders.
Tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back.
Press the forearms down and lift the shoulders away from the floor.
Walk the feet in slightly and keep the knees bent if needed.
Hold, then lower the knees.
breathing: Even breaths.
beginner_modification: Keep the knees bent.
advanced_variation: Walk the feet closer toward the elbows.
safety_tips: Keep the forearms parallel.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
benefits: Strengthens the arms and back
Opens the chest and the front of the hips
Part of the classic sun salutation
instructions: Lie on your front with the hands beside the lower ribs.
Press the tops of the feet down and straighten the arms, lifting the chest.
Lift the thighs off the floor if you can, so only the hands and feet touch the mat.
Draw the shoulders back and down and keep the neck long.
Hold for a breath or two, then lower or press back to Downward Dog.
breathing: Inhale into the pose.
beginner_modification: Keep the thighs down, or practise Cobra instead.
advanced_variation: Hold longer with the legs strongly engaged.
safety_tips: Keep the elbows soft if they hyperextend.

name: Camel Pose
benefits: Opens the chest and front of the body
Stretches the hip flexors and thighs
Strengthens the back
instructions: Kneel with the knees hip width apart and the thighs vertical.
Place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Lift the chest and gently lean back, keeping the hips over the knees.
If comfortable, reach the hands to the heels one at a time.
Keep the neck long or let the head release back only if comfortable. Come up slowly with the hands on the back.
breathing: Breathe into the chest; avoid holding the breath.
beginner_modification: Keep the hands on the lower back, or tuck the toes to lift the heels higher.
advanced_variation: Reach both hands to the heels with the feet flat.
common_mistakes: Hips drifting back behind the knees
safety_tips: Come out slowly and rest in Child's Pose.

name: Bow Pose
benefits: Strengthens the back
Stretches the front of the body from the knees to the chest
Opens the shoulders
instructions: Lie on your front and bend your knees, bringing the heels toward your hips.
Reach back and hold the outsides of the ankles.
Breathe in and kick the feet into the hands, lifting the chest and thighs.
Keep the knees about hip width apart and the neck long.
Hold, then release slowly.
breathing: Breathe steadily; the belly may rock with the breath.
beginner_modification: Hold one ankle at a time (half bow) or use a strap.
advanced_variation: Lift higher by pressing the feet into the hands.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of pressing with the legs
safety_tips: Keep the lift moderate at first.

name: Pigeon Pose
target_areas: Outer hip and glutes of the front leg
Hip flexors of the back leg
benefits: Deeply stretches the outer hip and glutes
Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg
Folding forward can feel calming
instructions: From Downward Dog or tabletop, bring the right knee forward behind the right wrist.
Angle the right shin across the mat; the closer to parallel with the front edge, the deeper it is.
Slide the left leg straight back with the top of the foot down.
Keep the hips level, using a blanket under the right hip if needed.
Stay upright on the hands or fold forward onto the forearms. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Long exhales help the hip release.
beginner_modification: Practise Reclined Pigeon (figure four) on your back instead.
advanced_variation: Fold all the way down with the arms extended.
common_mistakes: Sinking all the weight onto one side
safety_tips: Back off if you feel any pain in the front knee.

name: Reclined Pigeon
benefits: A gentle, controllable hip stretch
Kind to the knees compared with Pigeon
Good after running or sitting
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat.
Cross the right ankle over the left thigh, just below the knee.
Lift the left foot and hold behind the left thigh.
Draw the legs toward you until you feel a stretch in the right hip.
Hold, then switch sides.
breathing: Relax the hip on each exhale.
beginner_modification: Keep the bottom foot on the floor.
advanced_variation: Hold the bottom shin instead of the thigh.
safety_tips: Keep the crossed foot flexed to protect the knee.

name: Head-to-Knee Pose
target_areas: Inner thigh of the bent leg
benefits: Stretches one hamstring at a time
Gently rotates and lengthens the spine
A quiet, calming forward fold
instructions: Sit with the legs straight, then bend the left knee and place the left sole against the inner right thigh.
Turn the chest slightly toward the right leg.
Breathe in and lengthen the spine with the arms up.
Breathe out and fold over the right leg, holding the shin, ankle or foot.
Hold, then switch sides.
breathing: Fold a little deeper on each exhale.
beginner_modification: Sit on a blanket, bend the straight knee or use a strap.
advanced_variation: Hold the foot with both hands.
common_mistakes: Rounding the upper back to reach
safety_tips: Never force the fold.
contraindications: Knee injury of the bent leg

name: Seated Spinal Twist
benefits: Rotates the spine and improves its mobility
Stretches the outer hip and glutes
Encourages an upright seated posture
instructions: Sit tall with the legs straight.
Bend the right knee and place the right foot outside the left thigh.
Bend the left leg so the left heel rests near the right hip, or keep it straight.
Breathe in and lengthen the spine; breathe out and twist to the right, hooking the left elbow outside the right knee.
Place the right hand behind you. Lengthen on each inhale, twist gently on each exhale. Switch sides.
breathing: Grow taller on the inhale, twist on the exhale.
beginner_modification: Keep the bottom leg straight and hug the knee with the arm.
advanced_variation: Bind the hands behind the back.
safety_tips: Twist only as far as you can while keeping the spine long.

name: Revolved Chair
benefits: Combines leg strength with a spinal twist
Works the obliques
Builds heat and focus
instructions: Come into Chair Pose with the feet together.
Bring the palms together at the chest.
Breathe out and twist to the right, hooking the left elbow outside the right thigh.
Keep the knees level and the hips square.
Hold, return to centre and twist to the left.
breathing: Lengthen on the inhale, twist on the exhale.
beginner_modification: Keep the hands in prayer without hooking the elbow, or sit higher.
advanced_variation: Open the arms with one hand to the floor.
safety_tips: Twist from the ribs, not by forcing with the arm.

name: Dancer Pose
target_areas: Quadriceps and hip flexors of the lifted leg
benefits: Challenges balance and focus
Stretches the front of the lifted thigh and hip
Opens the chest and shoulders
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift onto the right foot.
Bend the left knee and hold the inside of the left ankle with the left hand.
Reach the right arm forward and up.
Kick the left foot into the hand and slowly tip the chest forward as the leg lifts behind you.
Keep the hips square and gaze forward. Return slowly and switch sides.
breathing: Calm breaths; use the exhale to steady yourself.
beginner_modification: Hold a wall with the front hand and keep the knee lower.
advanced_variation: Lift the back foot higher.
common_mistakes: Back knee swinging out to the side
safety_tips: Use a wall for support.

name: Fish Pose
benefits: Opens the chest and the front of the neck
Counters a hunched posture
Makes room for fuller breaths
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight.
Slide the hands under the hips, palms down, and draw the elbows in.
Press into the forearms and lift the chest.
Let the head tilt back gently, only resting the crown on the floor if comfortable.
Hold, then lift the head, lower the chest and rest.
breathing: Breathe into the upper chest.
beginner_modification: Lie back over a rolled blanket or block between the shoulder blades.
advanced_variation: Lift the legs a few inches.
safety_tips: Keep the weight in the forearms, not the head.

name: Reclined Bound Angle
benefits: A restful hip opener
Opens the chest with the arms relaxed
Good for winding down before sleep
instructions: Lie on your back and bring the soles of your feet together, letting the knees fall open.
Place cushions or blocks under the knees for support.
Rest the arms out to the sides or one hand on the belly and one on the chest.
Close your eyes and relax.
breathing: Slow belly breathing.
beginner_modification: Support each knee and lie on a bolster.
advanced_variation: Remove the support under the knees.
safety_tips: Support the knees if the inner thighs strain.

name: Crow Pose
benefits: Builds arm, wrist and core strength
Teaches balance on the hands
A confidence building first arm balance
instructions: Squat with the feet together and the knees wide; place the hands shoulder width apart on the mat.
Bend the elbows back and place the knees high on the backs of the upper arms.
Lean forward, shifting the weight into the hands, and look slightly ahead.
Lift one foot, then the other, drawing the heels toward the hips.
Hold, then lower the feet with control.
breathing: Keep breathing; exhale as you lean forward.
beginner_modification: Keep the toes on a block and lift one foot at a time.
advanced_variation: Straighten the arms (crane).
common_mistakes: Looking straight down and tipping forward
safety_tips: Place a cushion in front of your face while learning.

name: Wheel Pose
benefits: A deep backbend that opens the shoulders, chest and hips
Strengthens the arms, legs and back
Builds on Bridge Pose
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet hip width apart, close to the hips.
Place the hands beside the ears with the fingers pointing toward the shoulders.
Press into the hands and feet and lift onto the crown of the head, keeping the elbows in.
Straighten the arms and lift the head, pressing the chest toward the wall behind you.
Lower slowly by tucking the chin and placing the upper back down first. Rest with the knees hugged.
breathing: Keep breathing; avoid holding the breath.
beginner_modification: Stay in Bridge Pose or use two blocks against a wall under the hands.
advanced_variation: Walk the hands and feet closer.
common_mistakes: Dumping all the bend into the lower back
safety_tips: Warm up well with Bridge, Camel and shoulder openers first.
Come down slowly; never collapse onto the neck.
contraindications: Back, neck, wrist or shoulder injury
High blood pressure or heart conditions

name: Supported Headstand
benefits: Builds shoulder and core strength
Trains balance and body awareness upside down
A classic inversion for experienced practitioners
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
Kneel and place the forearms on the mat with the fingers interlaced and the elbows shoulder width apart.
Place the back of the head into the cupped hands, with the top of the head lightly on the mat.
Lift the knees and walk the feet in until the hips are over the shoulders.
Draw the knees in and lift the feet with control, then slowly straighten the legs up.
Press firmly through the forearms so very little weight is on the head. Come down the same way and rest in Child's Pose.
breathing: Smooth breathing; come down if the breath becomes strained.
beginner_modification: Practise Dolphin Pose, or learn with your back to a wall and a teacher present.
advanced_variation: Hold longer away from the wall.
common_mistakes: Weight on the head and neck
safety_tips: Learn with a qualified teacher.
The forearms carry the weight, not the neck.
Never practise on a soft bed or hard floor without a mat.
contraindications: High blood pressure, heart conditions, glaucoma or eye problems

name: Supported Shoulder Stand
benefits: An inversion that many people find calming
Strengthens the shoulders and core
Usually paired with Plow and Fish
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
Lie on your back with folded blankets under the shoulders and the head on the floor.
Bend the knees and lift the hips, supporting the back with the hands.
Walk the hands toward the shoulder blades and straighten the legs up.
Keep the weight on the shoulders and upper arms, never on the neck; do not turn the head.
Come down slowly by bending the knees and rolling down one vertebra at a time.
breathing: Breathe gently; the throat feels compressed, so keep it soft.
beginner_modification: Practise Legs Up the Wall instead.
advanced_variation: Release the hands to the floor.
safety_tips: Use folded blankets under the shoulders to protect the neck.
Never turn the head while inverted.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma or eye problems

name: Plow Pose
benefits: Stretches the whole back of the body
Often taught as a calming inversion
A counter stretch after backbends
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
From Supported Shoulder Stand, slowly lower the feet over your head toward the floor.
Keep the toes tucked and the legs straight, or rest the feet on a chair or blocks.
Keep supporting the back with the hands or interlace them on the floor.
Keep the neck still and the throat soft.
Roll down slowly with control.
breathing: Gentle breaths.
beginner_modification: Rest the feet on a chair seat behind your head.
advanced_variation: Bend the knees toward the ears (ear pressure pose).
safety_tips: Use blankets under the shoulders.

name: Handstand (at a wall)
benefits: Builds strong shoulders, arms and core
Trains balance upside down
Progressive and measurable practice
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
Place the hands shoulder width apart about a hand's length from a wall.
Come into a short Downward Dog and lift one leg.
Bend the standing knee and hop lightly, swinging the lifted leg up toward the wall.
Bring both heels to the wall, press the floor away and draw the ribs in.
Come down one leg at a time and rest in Child's Pose.
breathing: Steady breathing; come down if you feel strain.
beginner_modification: Practise Dolphin and L shaped handstand with the feet on the wall.
advanced_variation: Float the heels away from the wall.
common_mistakes: Hands too far from the wall
safety_tips: Always practise at a wall at first.
Learn to cartwheel out safely.
contraindications: High blood pressure or eye conditions

name: Front Splits
target_areas: Hip flexors of the back leg
benefits: A long term flexibility goal for the hamstrings and hip flexors
Builds patience and body awareness
Measurable progress with blocks
instructions: Practise this only after the intermediate poses feel steady, ideally with a qualified teacher.
Warm up with Low Lunge and Half Splits (front leg straight, hips over the back knee).
From Low Lunge, place blocks under the hands and slowly slide the front heel forward.
Let the back leg slide back with the knee pointing down, keeping the hips square.
Stop where you feel a strong but comfortable stretch and support the hips with a block or bolster.
Come out slowly by bending the front knee. Repeat on the other side.
breathing: Slow, long breaths; never force the stretch.
beginner_modification: Stay in Half Splits, or support the hips on a bolster.
advanced_variation: Lower fully and raise the arms.
safety_tips: Use blocks and stop well before pain.
Progress over weeks, not in one session.
